title: Academic and professional writing
summary: Writing like a researcher or a professional: impersonal se and the modest plural, hedging, the parts of a paper, formal connectors, reporting verbs, and formal letters and e-mails.
focus: The conventions, connectors and stance of academic and professional Spanish
content:
## The impersonal voice

Academic Spanish keeps the writer in the background.

- **Passive se** agrees with the thing: **Se analizaron cuarenta encuestas** (not *se analizó cuarenta encuestas*).
- **Impersonal se** with people and **a** stays singular: **Se entrevistó a veinte docentes.**
- **The modest plural** (**plural de modestia**): a single author writes **analizamos**, **consideramos**, **en este trabajo proponemos**. Keep it consistent from the first page to the last.

The **nominal style** strings nouns together: *la realización de un análisis de la evolución de los precios*. A little sounds formal; a lot sounds like a form. Turn nouns back into verbs: **analizamos cómo evolucionaron los precios**.

## Hedging and stance

A careful writer claims exactly what the data allow.

| instead of | write |
|---|---|
| *Es obvio que…* | **Cabe pensar que…**, **Todo indica que…** |
| *Los datos demuestran…* | **Los datos parecen indicar…**, **sugieren…** |
| *Siempre, nunca* | **En la mayoría de los casos**, **rara vez** |

**Cabe señalar / destacar que…** (it should be noted that) flags a point; **cabría pensar que…** (one might think that) raises an idea you may then reject; **en cierta medida** (to some extent) limits a claim.

## Structure and connectors

A paper usually runs **introducción**, **estado de la cuestión** (what others have said), **metodología**, **resultados**, **conclusiones**.

| function | connectors |
|---|---|
| add | **asimismo**, **además**, **por otra parte** |
| contrast | **no obstante**, **sin embargo**, **ahora bien** |
| consequence | **por consiguiente**, **por lo tanto**, **de ahí que** + subjunctive |
| topic | **en lo que respecta a**, **en cuanto a** |
| basis | **a tenor de** (in the light of), **de acuerdo con** |
| close | **en definitiva**, **en suma** |

## Reporting other voices

Choose the verb that says what the source does with its idea:

- **sostiene** (maintains), **afirma** (states): the author defends it.
- **señala** (points out), **advierte** (warns): the author draws attention to it.
- **matiza** (qualifies): the author accepts it with limits.
- **refuta** (refutes): the author shows it is wrong.
- **plantea** (raises, proposes): the author puts it forward.

*García sostiene que el modelo funciona; López lo matiza, y Ortega lo refuta con datos nuevos.*

## Letters, e-mails and one gerund to avoid

- Open with **Estimada señora Ruiz:** or **Estimado señor López:** (a colon, not a comma). **Le escribo para…** states the purpose.
- Close with **Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.** and **Atentamente,** or **Un cordial saludo,**.
- Avoid the gerund that describes a noun or a later event, common in official texts: *Se aprobó una ley regulando el alquiler* becomes **una ley que regula el alquiler**.

vocabulary.example: Cabe señalar que la muestra es pequeña.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It should be noted that the sample is small.

vocabulary.example: Cabría pensar que el precio influye, pero los datos no lo confirman.
vocabulary.example_meaning: One might think that price has an influence, but the data don't confirm it.

vocabulary.example: El aumento de las ventas parece indicar un cambio de tendencia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The rise in sales seems to indicate a change in trend.

vocabulary.meaning: literature review, state of the art
vocabulary.example: El estado de la cuestión ocupa todo el segundo capítulo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The literature review takes up the whole second chapter.

vocabulary.example: La metodología combina entrevistas y encuestas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The methodology combines interviews and surveys.

vocabulary.example: El estudio es sólido; no obstante, la muestra es reducida.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The study is sound; nevertheless, the sample is small.

vocabulary.example: Asimismo, se revisaron los informes de los últimos cinco años.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Likewise, the reports from the last five years were reviewed.

vocabulary.example: Los costes subieron y, por consiguiente, la obra se retrasó.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Costs rose and, consequently, the building work was delayed.

vocabulary.example: En lo que respecta a la financiación, no ha habido cambios.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As regards funding, there have been no changes.

vocabulary.meaning: in the light of, according to
vocabulary.example: A tenor de los resultados, conviene revisar la hipótesis.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In the light of the results, the hypothesis should be revised.

vocabulary.example: La autora sostiene que el modelo ha quedado obsoleto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The author maintains that the model has become obsolete.

vocabulary.meaning: to qualify, to add nuance to
vocabulary.example: En la entrevista, el ministro matizó sus palabras del lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In the interview, the minister qualified what he had said on Monday.

vocabulary.example: El segundo experimento refuta la hipótesis inicial.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The second experiment disproves the initial hypothesis.

vocabulary.meaning: to look forward to, to await (formal letters)
vocabulary.example: Quedamos a la espera de su confirmación.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We look forward to your confirmation.

quiz.explanation: Passive se agrees with the thing: cuarenta encuestas is plural, so se analizaron. With people and a, the verb would stay singular: se entrevistó a veinte docentes.
hints: What is plural in the sentence?

quiz.prompt: ___ señalar que la muestra es reducida. (It should be noted…)
quiz.explanation: Cabe + infinitive (cabe señalar, cabe destacar) is the formal way to flag a point: it should be noted that…
No obstante = nevertheless. Asimismo adds a point and por consiguiente introduces a consequence.

quiz.prompt: Los costes se duplicaron y, por ___, el proyecto se canceló.
quiz.explanation: Por consiguiente (consequently) introduces a result. Por consecuente is a common slip.

quiz.prompt: La autora ___ que la hipótesis es correcta, aunque otros estudios la ponen en duda. (maintains)
quiz.explanation: Sostener means to maintain, so she defends the hypothesis. Refutar would mean she shows it is wrong; matizar, that she accepts it with limits.

quiz.prompt: En lo que ___ a la financiación, no ha habido cambios.
quiz.explanation: The fixed connector is en lo que respecta a (as regards). En lo que respecto a is a frequent error.
hints: The verb is respectar, third person.

quiz.prompt: Which is the right opening for a formal e-mail to Dr Marta Ruiz?
quiz.explanation: Formal letters open with Estimado / Estimada and a colon. Querida is for people you know well, and Spanish uses a colon, not a comma, after the greeting.
hints: Formal adjective, and the punctuation Spanish uses after a greeting.

quiz.prompt: Choose the better version for an official text.
options: Se aprobó una ley que regula el alquiler de temporada.
Se aprobó una ley regulando el alquiler de temporada.
quiz.correct_answer: Se aprobó una ley que regula el alquiler de temporada.
quiz.explanation: A gerund should not describe a noun like an adjective clause. Una ley que regula… is correct; una ley regulando… is a classic flaw of official prose.
hints: Can a gerund work like 'which regulates'?

quiz.prompt: A ___ de los resultados, conviene revisar la hipótesis. (In the light of…)
quiz.explanation: A tenor de means in the light of or according to. It is a formal way to base a conclusion on something.

quiz.prompt: Quedamos ___ espera de que nos confirmen la fecha de entrega.
quiz.explanation: Quedar a la espera de takes a noun (de su respuesta) or de que + subjunctive: quedamos a la espera de que nos confirmen… (we look forward to your confirming…). The plural quedamos speaks for a company.
hints: A preposition and an article, built on the noun espera.
It is the classic closing of a formal e-mail.

listening.text: Cabe destacar el papel de los voluntarios.
listening.meaning: The role of the volunteers deserves to be highlighted.
listening.note: Cabe + infinitive is a formal way to flag a point.

listening.text: Asimismo, se entrevistó a veinte docentes.
No obstante, los resultados deben interpretarse con cautela.
listening.meaning: Nevertheless, the results must be interpreted with caution.

listening.text: En este trabajo analizamos tres modelos de gestión.
listening.meaning: In this paper we analyse three management models.
listening.note: This is the modest plural, one author using the nosotros form.

listening.text: La autora matiza su conclusión en el último capítulo.
listening.meaning: The author qualifies her conclusion in the last chapter.

listening.text: Los datos parecen indicar que el consumo ha bajado ligeramente.
listening.meaning: The data seem to indicate that consumption has fallen slightly.

listening.text: Le escribo para solicitar información sobre la convocatoria de becas.
listening.meaning: I am writing to request information about the call for scholarship applications.
listening.note: New word: la convocatoria = the call for applications.

listening.text: Sin otro particular, quedo a la espera de su respuesta y le saludo atentamente.
listening.meaning: With nothing further to add, I look forward to your reply. Yours faithfully.

guide.tip: Before you hand in a text, underline every es obvio, siempre and demuestra. Most of them want a hedge.

conversations.title: Feedback on chapter two
conversations.scenario: Irene, a thesis supervisor, gives Daniel, her PhD student, feedback on the second chapter of his thesis.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Daniel, he leído el segundo capítulo. El estado de la cuestión está muy completo.
lines.meaning: Daniel, I've read the second chapter. The literature review is very thorough.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Gracias. Noto que viene un pero.
lines.meaning: Thanks. I can feel a 'but' coming.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No obstante, abusas del estilo nominal: la realización de la medición de los datos.
lines.meaning: Nevertheless, you overuse the nominal style: la realización de la medición de los datos.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Sería mejor decir simplemente medimos los datos?
lines.meaning: Would it be better to say simply medimos los datos?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Exacto. Y mantén el plural de modestia en todo el capítulo, no solo a ratos.
lines.meaning: Exactly. And keep the modest plural throughout the chapter, not just now and then.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: De acuerdo. ¿Y las conclusiones? ¿Son demasiado tajantes?
lines.meaning: All right. And the conclusions? Are they too categorical?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Un poco. Escribes que los resultados demuestran la hipótesis. Yo lo matizaría: parecen indicar.
lines.meaning: A little. You write that the results prove the hypothesis. I would qualify it: they seem to indicate.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Cabría pensar que así la tesis pierde fuerza.
lines.meaning: One might think the thesis loses strength that way.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Al contrario: gana credibilidad. Un tribunal desconfía de las certezas absolutas.
lines.meaning: On the contrary: it gains credibility. An examining panel distrusts absolute certainties.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Entendido. Lo reviso esta semana y te lo envío el viernes.
lines.meaning: Understood. I'll revise it this week and send it to you on Friday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Perfect. I'll look out for it.

bites.title: Se: agree or not?
bites.rule: Passive se agrees with the thing: se analizaron cuarenta encuestas. With people introduced by a, the verb stays singular: se entrevistó a veinte docentes.

bites.title: Hedge, don't shout
bites.rule: Claim what the data allow: cabe señalar, cabría pensar, parece indicar, en cierta medida. Es obvio que and demuestra rarely survive peer review.
bites.example: Los datos parecen indicar un cambio de tendencia.
bites.example_meaning: The data seem to indicate a change in trend.

bites.title: The right reporting verb
bites.rule: Sostiene = maintains, señala = points out, matiza = qualifies, refuta = refutes, plantea = raises. The verb tells the reader what the source does with the idea.
bites.example: Pérez plantea una hipótesis que Ortega refuta.
bites.example_meaning: Pérez puts forward a hypothesis that Ortega refutes.

bites.title: Formal letters
bites.rule: Open with Estimada señora Ruiz: (a colon, not a comma), state the purpose with Le escribo para…, close with Quedo a la espera de su respuesta and Atentamente.
bites.example: Le escribo para solicitar una prórroga.
bites.example_meaning: I am writing to request an extension.

sorts.title: What does the connector do?
sorts.why: Asimismo and además add; no obstante and sin embargo contrast; por consiguiente and en definitiva draw a consequence or a conclusion.

sorts.title: Academic, or too casual?
sorts.why: Academic prose hedges and names its topic formally; chatty openers and absolute claims belong in conversation.

spots.sentence: Se analizó cuarenta encuestas en tres ciudades.
spots.why: Passive se agrees with the plural thing: se analizaron cuarenta encuestas.

spots.sentence: Se aprobó un decreto regulando los alquileres.
spots.why: A gerund cannot describe a noun; use a relative clause.

spots.sentence: Los costes subieron y, por consecuente, la obra se retrasó.
En lo que respecto a la financiación, no hubo cambios.
spots.why: The fixed connector is en lo que respecta a.

spots.sentence: Quedo en la espera de su respuesta.
spots.why: The formula is quedo a la espera de.

builds.meaning: It should be noted that the sample is small.

builds.text: No obstante, los datos son limitados.
Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
builds.meaning: I look forward to your reply.

builds.text: La autora sostiene una tesis distinta.
builds.meaning: The author maintains a different thesis.
